lines: I came back to my work. That feels smaller than victory and better than a monument.
The village sounds normal again, which is how I know I am still <shake>shaking</shake>.
I survived. Now I get to do chores, which is a strange kind of mercy.
It fits into ordinary work better than I expected. That is a compliment.
Good gear does not feel heroic. It feels like one less thing waiting to go wrong.
I kept it close. Around here, useful gifts become habits.
You helped keep tomorrow ordinary. That is not a small thing.
The village still has chores because you helped it survive long enough to need them.
I heard the fighting. Then I heard doors opening again. <pulse>Thank you.</pulse>
I woke up wanting to work again. That is how I knew I was back.
My hands remembered their trade before my thoughts stopped <shake>trembling</shake>.
You gave me a morning I did not think I would see.
An apology is a repair. Do not hand me a tool you will not use.
I can respect a crack that admits it is a crack. Now prove it will not spread.
Words are the first patch. <bold>Behavior</bold> is the stitching.
I hear you. The village will need more than hearing.
Apologies are seeds. We will see what <pulse>grows</pulse>.
I want to believe you. Help make that less foolish.
A new little voice joined us. Even the work sounded softer for a while.
There is a baby in the village now. Everyone pretends not to smile and fails.
New life makes the whole place count its <pulse>blessings</pulse> out loud.
Night came too close. We will be checking latches before sunset for a while.
The dark tested the village and found us awake enough.
I heard the thing outside before I saw it. That is the part sleep <shake>remembers</shake>.
You helped chase danger from our doors. Ordinary work feels possible again.
The village saw you stand with us. That sort of thing travels faster than gossip.
Because of you, today still has chores instead of <italic>funerals</italic>.
You fought during the raid. Some debts are too large for emeralds.
I saw you answer the bell. <bold>That matters here.</bold>
When raiders came, you did not treat us like someone else's problem.
Fire makes every bucket feel too small until the smoke thins.
We checked walls, roofs, hands, and tempers. Fire leaves marks on all of them.
A village learns the value of water very quickly when flame gets ideas.
The weather had teeth today. We kept close to doors and counted heads twice.
Storms make the village smaller for a while. Smaller can be safer.
I do not mind weather with manners. That was not weather with manners.
Taking from a village chest is not clever. It is loud in a way locks cannot show.
We remember what was taken, and we remember who made us count.
Trust is stored in ordinary places too. Chests, mostly.
Someone was hurt. The village has been listening differently since.
After an attack, even familiar footsteps need a moment to become familiar again.
We are still here, but the day is not as soft as it was.
